title: Influence of glucose concentration in tissue on the ability to drive in patients with diabetes
summary: The purpose of the pilot study is to investigate whether there is a correlation between driving ability and glucose concentration in tissue in the normal range (>80 mg/dl) and heart rate. For this purpose, patients with insulin-dependent diabetes complete a 60-minute driving training in a driving simulator in 3 blocks of 20 minutes with increasing difficulty. The tissue glucose concentration is continuously measured and the heart rate is recorded. Possible driving errors are recorded via the driving simulator. A survey about the individual stress level is carried out after each driving block.

interventions.name: Patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus complete a driving training in a driving simulator, while data on glucose concentration in tissue, heart rate and driving performance are continuously collected.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
insulin-dependet diabetes mellitus type I or II
diriving license
Exclusion criteria:
lack of ability to give consent, 
lack to follow the study procedure
language barrier
lack of physical ability to operate the driving simulator
pregnancy
severe metabolic imbalance
unstable CHD
